answer_1.quote: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to simulate human behavior, with promising results in replicating individual decisions in cognitive science tasks.
answer_1.outputs: LLM agents simulate human participants in a multi-stage group decision task involving deliberation, self-nomination, and leader election.

answer_2.quote: We introduce and measure the optimal leader gap—the performance gap between the elected leader and the best possible candidate—and examine whether this gap stems from self-exclusion (the best candidate not nominating) or peer-exclusion (the group not electing them).

answer_4.quote: Participants were recruited via Prolific under IRB-approved protocols. 824 individuals enrolled and were randomly assigned to either HI or HP.
answer_4.guideline: Participants completed a survival task involving group discussion, self-nomination, and leader election, with performance determining group reward. Post-task survey included questions on prior experience, risk willingness, and gender beliefs.
